summary: accounts reconcile now defaults since_date to 2000-01-01 (effectively full account history) instead of leaving it unset, so the candidate-transaction search is no longer silently capped at YNAB's one-year default lookback.
reason: The prior patch (ynab-novel-command-freshness) only documented the one-year-lookback limitation in result.Note when --since-date was omitted; it did not fix the underlying gap. Greptile's follow-up review of PR #1725 (confidence 4/5, 'not yet safe to merge') confirmed the command's whole purpose is finding the transaction responsible for a statement discrepancy, and that transaction can predate the one-year window on any account with longer history, at which point it silently never appears in candidates even though the difference itself (computed from the account's real all-time cleared_balance) is correct.
validated_outcome: When --since-date is omitted, the transaction fetch now explicitly passes since_date=2000-01-01 rather than omitting the parameter, so YNAB's API no longer applies its own one-year default. result.Note's caveat was inverted to only fire when the user themselves narrows the window with --since-date. go build ./..., go vet ./..., and go test ./internal/cli/... (including TestNovelAccountsReconcileHelpWires) all clean.
